tasks.description: Map aqi_uk (1–10) to UK DAQI bands (Low:1–3, Moderate:4–6, High:7–9, Very High:10) and attach a simple risk label.
Compute a short-term trend on aqi_uk using a lightweight 3-point slope or last-value vs previous-mean comparison and label as rising/falling/steady.
Calculate exceedance ratios against WHO 2021 short-term guidelines (e.g., PM2.5:15, PM10:45, NO2:25, SO2:40, O3:100, CO:4000 µg/m3) and identify the dominant pollutant per timestamp.
Compute PM2.5/PM10 ratio and classify likely particle source mix: >0.6 (fine/combustion), 0.3–0.6 (mixed), <0.3 (coarse dust).
Aggregate by hour-of-day over the last 24–48 hours and report the peak hour for PM2.5 and O3 (handles sparse data gracefully).
Detect duplicate rows (identical timestamps/components) and stuck sensors (unchanged readings across N intervals) and report counts and percentages.
Verify actual sampling gaps against the expected 10–15 minute interval; flag missing/late data and compute basic uptime metrics.
Trigger a lightweight alert when PM2.5 exhibits a sudden spike between consecutive readings (e.g., >10 µg/m3 absolute or >25% relative increase).
Generate brief, on-device health advisories for general and sensitive groups based on DAQI band and the identified dominant pollutant.
Compute a 24-hour time-weighted mean of PM2.5 using actual timestamp gaps (handles 10–15 min irregularity), require >=60% coverage, and classify against WHO 24h guideline (15 µg/m3).
Estimate near-real-time PM2.5 using the US EPA NowCast (up to last 12 samples): w = max(0.5, 1 - (max-min)/max); compute weighted mean and label low/moderate/high.
Compute NOx = NO + NO2 and the O3/NOx ratio; classify regime as traffic-dominated (low ratio), mixed, or photochemically aged (high ratio).
Validate lat/lon against metadata ranges and flag sensor relocation/drift if step change >0.01° or out-of-bounds values are observed.
Compare CSV headers with metadata definitions; flag missing/extra fields, duplicate entries, and name mismatches (e.g., o3 vs no3), and suggest a mapping fix.
Sum minutes above WHO short-term guidelines (PM2.5:15, PM10:45, NO2:25, SO2:40, O3:100, CO:4000 µg/m3) over the last 24h per pollutant; report top offender.
Flag sustained episodes when any pollutant exceeds its guideline for N consecutive readings (default N=3), to distinguish persistent pollution from brief spikes.
Recommend whether it’s currently safe to ventilate based on PM2.5 and O3 staying below thresholds for the last M intervals (e.g., M=2–3) and no recent spike detected.
